title: Border-aware routing exceptions and graceful fallback heuristics for EU residency
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a border-aware routing layer that enforces EU-only data residency constraints while supporting customer-level allowlists/denylists and deterministic fallback to regional model variants. The goal is to ensure requests from EU-scoped customers never leave EU-backed infrastructure unless explicitly allowed, and when capacity or variant incompatibility occurs the system performs a predictable, auditable fallback that minimizes both data egress and customer disruption.
acceptance_criteria: Requests tagged with customer.residency=EU are routed only to EU-backed instances (hosted or private) unless customer override is present
Customer allowlist entries allow explicit cross-border routing and are stored in tenant config with audit logging
Customer denylist entries prevent specific model variants or tiers from being used for the tenant

Fallback hierarchy implemented: in-region same-variant -> in-region compatible-variant (quantized/low-memory) -> queued retry with backoff -> policy-mode fallback (customer-allow or emergency-cross-border), each step logged with reason codes
End-to-end integration test coverage for routing decisions, including simulated EU capacity outage and allowlist/denylist resolution
Tracing and dashboard surfaces in Console: per-request policy decision, resolution path, and latency/cost delta
Security review completed and audit log retention configured per compliance requirements
design_decisions: Policy precedence: tenant residency override > tenant allowlist/denylist > account-level residency policy > global emergency-deny
Store policy artifacts (allow/deny lists, residency flags) in customer-config service with versioned records and immutable audit events
Use a compact decision code (e.g., DEC=EU_ONLY, DEC=ALLOW_OVERRIDE, DEC=FALLBACK_COMPAT_MODEL, DEC=EMERGENCY_CROSS_BORDER) for easy dashboarding and cheaper tracing payloads
Fallback behavior is configurable per-tenant: strict (never cross-border) | soft (cross-border with encryption+consent header) | permissive
Prefer in-region quantized/compatible variants rather than immediate cross-border routing to minimize legal exposure and latency variance
Expose a 'policy-explain' header on responses for debugging and customer support (redacts PII)
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Policy store schema updates (versioned allow/deny entries, residency flags, per-tenant fallback mode)
Phase 2: Decision service changes: add EU-only gate, match against allowlist/denylist, produce decision code and preferred route set
Phase 3: Router integration: enforce decision codes in SmartRouter; add circuit-breaker on region capacity and trigger fallback sequence
Phase 4: Model catalog tagging: mark model variants by residency-compliance and compatibility (compat-tags)
Phase 5: Console/UI: tenant policy editor, decision audit viewer, and rollout controls
Phase 6: Integration tests, chaos tests (simulate EU region loss), and performance regression testing
Phase 7: Gradual rollout with canary on non-production tenants, then opt-in customers, then global rollout with emergency-deny safety gate
tests: Unit: decision service resolves allow/deny precedence and returns expected decision codes
Integration: SmartRouter honors decision codes and does not route EU-residency requests outside EU unless allow override present
End-to-end: simulate capacity drop in eu-west and validate fallback path selects in-region compatible variant before cross-border option
Security: audit log generation and tamper-evidence check, retention policy verification
Load: throughput under combined policy-check + routing under peak traffic with prefix caching enabled
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Strict residency may cause increased 503s during EU capacity exhaustion. Mitigation: implement backoff queue + notify customer via SLA event and recommend Dedicated reservation
Risk: Allowlist misuse could cause legal exposure. Mitigation: require signed customer consent for cross-border override and record signed consent in config store
Risk: Decision service is a new critical path for every request. Mitigation: add local cache in router nodes with short TTL and incremental invalidation on policy changes
Risk: Complexity of variant compatibility mapping leads to incorrect fallback. Mitigation: add compatibility matrix tests and require model onboarding checklist to include compat-tags
